---
title: "What a LangSmith export must contain before anyone can review it"
description: "Screenshots are not an export. Absence of a stop field is not proof there was no stop rule."
date: 2026-08-31
author: "William Edgar Brissey"
categories: [agent-trace diagnostics, evidence, LangSmith]
---

Observability captured the run. That is not the same as a file someone else can inspect.

A review of an agent incident is only as strong as the export. Most "we have LangSmith" conversations still fail this test. The failure is usually not the model. It is the package.

## Screenshots are not an export

A screenshot proves that a UI existed at a moment. It does not give stable run IDs, order, tool payloads, or a hash of what was sent.

If the only artifact is a picture of the tracer, the honest next step is to produce a file — or to admit the system cannot.

## A reviewable package is small and named

One path. One window. Named start and end, or named run IDs. JSON or JSONL in a zip. No keys in the file. Secrets removed before the file leaves the account. A SHA-256 of the file as sent.

The hash proves the bits did not change in transit. It does not prove the bits were redacted.

## Fields that have to exist

- Stable run or trace ID on every included run
- Timestamps or another order that reconstructs the path
- Run type or name
- Status or error, or an explicit note that the vendor did not emit it
- Parent / session linkage, or an explicit note that this is one isolated run

If the complaint is a loop, retry, or overshoot, tool records have to be in the file — or the reviewer must not claim they saw the loop in the trace.

## Absence is evidence of absence in the file

A missing stop-condition field is not proof that the product had no stop rule. It is proof that this export does not contain one.

If you want a finding about a stop rule, attach the rule as text the owner supplies, or accept that the finding cannot be "the agent ignored the stop rule." It can only be "the export does not show a stop event."

## Refuse

Live dashboard logins. Org-wide dumps with no window. Unredacted secrets. An invoice with no traces offered as proof the model misbehaved.

JSON that parses is not the same as a path a human can reconstruct. If IDs, order, or tool records are missing, the correct outcome is not a guessed root cause. It is: correct the export, or stop.

This note is evidence hygiene. It is not an engagement and not a certificate.
